# Sāsanapaṭṭhāna (Ne 37)

**ID:** Ne 37
**Section:** Netti (ne)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-2
**Title (Pali):** Sāsanapaṭṭhāna
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0519m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* ("The Pattern of the Dispensation") constitutes the final subsection of the *Paṭiniddesavāra* ("Further Explanation") in the *Nettippakaraṇa*, following the *Hāravibhaṅga*, *Hārasampāta*, and *Nayasamuṭṭhāna* [Caudron 2000]. Within the hermeneutical framework of the *Netti*, it embodies an extensive classification and mapping of Piṭaka passages according to their leading themes and thoughts [Law 1923]. Because its categories and classifications extend beyond the basic method of sixteen modes (*hārā*) and five guide-lines (*nayā*) established in the *Uddesavāra*, scholars have examined whether this section was integral to the core interpretive methodology or represents a later stratum of commentary [Balasooriya et al. 1980; Caudron 2000].

 Machine-assisted analysis via DharmaNexus shows extensive Pali-internal text reuse with the commentary (*Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*) and subcommentary (*Nettivibhāvinī*), as well as a related chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, *Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi*) and numerous canonical discourses across the *Aṅguttara*, *Saṁyutta*, and *Dīgha Nikāyas* (such as AN 4, SN 35, SN 55, SN 12, AN 10, and DN 21) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments are also identified between passages in this text and Northern Buddhist works, including Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Udānavarga*, the *Patna Dharmapada*, Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā*, and Chinese Āgama translations including the *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and *Saṁyukta Āgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
